title.narrative: TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE FOR BUILDING CLIMATE RESILIENCE OF VULNERABLE HEALTH AND EDUCATION INFRASTRUCTURE

description.narrative: Mozambique is one of the countries in the world most exposed to natural threats, particularly hydro-meteorological threats and epidemics. The country has a vast record of droughts, floods, storms, and tropical cyclones, which have increased in frequency and intensity over the past four decades, putting at risk populations, livelihoods, economy, and vulnerable infrastructure. According to the 2021’s Global Climate Risk Index, Mozambique was the country most affected by climate change in 2019. Following cyclone Idai in 2019, Mozambique has been bit by additional 09 cyclones, the last being the Freddy Cyclone that hit the country twice in spam of Months, bringing to evidence the increase in frequency of climate related events. The post-cyclone Freddy emergency situation that affected Mozambique during the months of February and March 2023 resulted in the partial destruction of approximately 163 healthcare facilities and 4,430 classrooms in the provinces of Gaza, Inhambane, Sofala, Manica, Tete, Zambézia, and Niassa, affecting 1,187,265 people, by the first and second landfall, being 31% women, 22% men and 46% children. Women and girls are most at risk in disasters such as cyclones when there is a lack of clean water, sanitation and hygiene services, as they are usually responsible for collecting and managing household water supplies. The lack of water, soap and safe facilities for changing and washing also makes it difficult to manage menstrual health, which has led to many girls dropping out of schools destroyed by the cyclone. Amidst displacement and loss of livelihoods and essentials, pregnant women, many of whom were living in resettlement centres and temporary shelters, faced increased risks due to the cholera outbreak, compounded by the impact of Cyclone Freddy, which destroyed some health infrastructure with more impact the Zambezia province.It is estimated that 70 percent of schools in Mozambique are in high-risk areas. It has been shown that school infrastructure suffers more than US$2 million in damages per year (0,25% of overall annual education sector spending), which corresponds to 540 classrooms and 57,000 students affected annually Impact of climate events on health infrastructure is also high. In 2022, Cyclone Gombe destroyed well over 60 health facilities only in the Nampula province. With the passage of cyclone Freddy, and with the aim of ensuring the resilience of Education and Health infrastructure, the World Bank approved new funding to the Government of Mozambique through the Contingent Emergency Response Component, CERC, to support preparatory activities in response to the impact of cyclone Freddy. UN-Habitat have received a request from the World Bank and the Ministries of Health and Education of Mozambique to support both Ministries in the post-disaster recovery through the reconstruction of public infrastructures (schools and health centres). The proposal is to sign a Technical Assistance agreement with the Ministry of Health to support both Ministries. Also important is that this proposal is in line with the "Safer Schools" programme, which is now being expanded to the health sector, and also with an ongoing Technical Assistance project to the Government on school reconstruction in Mozambique. This proposal comes in a momentum where UN-Habitat have managed to build an enabling environment to accommodate the Government priorities in strengthening the country’s and communities resilience to climate shocks and stresses, through the approache of “living with floods and cyclones”, stressing the need of Adaptation. In such regard, in 2019, after Mozambique has been strongly hit by Cyclones Idai and Kenneth, UN Habitat Mozambique Country Office have developed the so-called Building Back Better and Resilience Building Umbrella Programme (2019-2024) with the overall objective to enhance the climate adaptation capacity of Mozambican people and institutions and achieve more resilient human settlements. The Umbrella Programme aims at working as a common and coherent framework that will guide UN-Habitat short, medium and long-term projects, programmes and engagements regarding the post-cyclone reconstruction. It is being operationalized through two complementary axes of interventions to support the recovery and reconstruction process in Mozambique: Axis 1- Building Back Better Safer (BBB) Schools, Hospitals and Resilient Housing and Axis 2 - Enhancing Urban Resilience through Integrated Approaches. In the same Year, UN-Habitat have signed a MoU with the Ministry of Health, and Idai Post Cyclone Reconstruction Cabinet (GREPOC)- timespam?. Also UN-Habitat has signed two AoC with the Ministry od Education.
